```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(rcupp)
```

`rcupp` is the low-level bridge to a fixed set of GPU linear algebra
operators. Most users will want the high-level `cudaGlmnet` package instead;
this vignette shows the raw solver entry point and how to read its result.

## A first fit

```{r fit}
set.seed(1)
X <- matrix(rnorm(50 * 5), 50, 5)
y <- drop(X %*% c(2, -1, 0, 0, 0)) + rnorm(50, sd = 0.3)

fit <- lasso_fista(X, y, lambda = 0.05)
fit$beta
```

The solver minimizes the Gaussian lasso objective
`1/(2n) * sum((y - X %*% b)^2) + lambda * sum(abs(b))`. It returns a list
with the coefficient vector and a few diagnostics:

```{r result}
fit$objective
fit$iterations
fit$converged
```

## Backend

`rcupp` can be built with a CUDA backend or with a CPU reference shim. The
same call and the same result shape apply in both cases; `cuda_available()`
only reports which one is linked.

```{r backend}
cuda_available()
fit$backend
```

No GPU is required to run this vignette. When the package was built without
the CUDA toolkit the solver uses the CPU shim and all examples still work.

## Where to go next

The `cudaGlmnet` package wraps this solver with a glmnet-like interface:
lambda paths, cross-validation, standardization and coef/predict methods.
Downstream packages can also call the public C operators directly through
`LinkingTo: rcupp`; see the repository's linking guide.
